role: Independent scope reviewer — verify contract integrity before implementation unfreeze
summary: Implementation scope is well-structured, internally consistent, and ready to proceed. Two P2 observations identified: (1) file organization divergence from parent design contract (thought_process.py merged into kernel.py), (2) confidence factor naming/weighting divergence from parent design. Neither is blocking — they represent implementation-level refinements of the architecture, but should be acknowledged and optionally reconciled with the design contract before implementation begins. All critical guards are in place: 24 files protected with zero overlap, import isolation rules cover the top-risk paths, memory adapter properly interfaces through rank_retrieve(), test coverage distributes correctly across module complexity.

observations.title: File organization divergence from parent design contract
observations.detail: Parent DESIGN_V1.json (line 271) lists thought_process.py as a separate file: 'brain/reasoning/kernel.py, context_assembler.py, thought_process.py, confidence.py, self_check.py, decision_framework.py'. IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_V1.json merges ThoughtProcessEngine as an inner class inside kernel.py. The implementation contract's approach is valid (inner class reduces file count and coupling concerns) but introduces a structural divergence from the architecture design.
observations.recommendation: Either update DESIGN_V1 to reflect the merged structure, or document this as an intentional implementation refinement in the contract diff.

observations.title: Confidence factor names and weights diverged from parent design
observations.detail: DESIGN_V1.json factors: evidence_strength(0.35), memory_quality(0.25), past_success_rate(0.20), reasoning_completeness(0.15), self_consistency(0.05). IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_V1.json factors: evidence_strength(0.35), consistency(0.20), completeness(0.20), source_reliability(0.15), historical_accuracy(0.10). Both sum to 1.0, but factor names and weights differ. The implementation contract's factors may be more testable (simpler factor names, no dependency on memory quality metrics which don't exist yet) but this is a significant semantic change.
observations.recommendation: Reconcile with design contract. If the implementation contract's factor set is intentional (better testability, avoids Phase 2 dependencies), explicitly document the rationale and update DESIGN_V1 accordingly.

brain_files_protected.note: 16 brain .py files exist on disk. 11 are explicitly protected. 5 auxiliary files (provenance.py, consolidation_rules.py, decay_config.py, brain_receipt.py, __init__.py) are not in the untouchable list but are not at risk — all new files go under the non-existent brain/reasoning/ subdirectory.

overlap_check.evidence: All 7 new Python files live under brain/reasoning/ (new subdirectory, confirmed absent on disk). All 13 runtime files live under src/nexara_prime/ (not brain/reasoning/). All 11 brain files live under brain/ (not brain/reasoning/). Zero namespace collision.

gaps.title: 5 absolute_prohibition files not explicitly covered by import prohibition rules
gaps.detail: The import_prohibition list (4 rules) covers runtime.py, evidence.py, evaluation.py, tools.py, model_gateway.py. The absolute_prohibition list also protects state_machine.py, governance.py, chief_brain_kernel.py, api.py, cli.py — but these are not explicitly in the import prohibition rules. While the absolute_prohibition says they cannot be modified (which is stronger than import prohibition), a reasoning developer could still import from them unintentionally. The contract should explicitly forbid importing from ALL 13 absolute_prohibition files.
gaps.recommendation: Add import prohibition rules for the remaining 5 runtime files, or add a blanket rule: 'brain/reasoning/ NEVER imports any module in the absolute_prohibition list.'

4_test_coverage.distribution_analysis: Thought Process (15) and Context Assembly (15) are the most complex modules (7-step chain, 6-step pipeline with 5 retrieval strategies respectively) — they receive the highest test allocation. Remaining modules receive 10 tests each, appropriate for single-method interfaces. Isolation tests (10) cover cross-cutting import boundary enforcement. Distribution is well-calibrated.
